introduction: Tailored for advanced legal exams and UPSC Mains, this level explores the absolute frontiers of Indian labor law. It covers the global-first statutory recognition of the Gig Economy, the paradigm shift in workplace inspections, and the extensive decriminalization of labor offenses.

core_concepts.title: Gig and Platform Workers (Code on Social Security)
core_concepts.description:
For the first time globally, India provides statutory recognition to 'Gig Workers' (those who earn outside a traditional employer-employee relationship) and 'Platform Workers' (those who use online platforms like Uber, Zomato, Swiggy).
- Funding Mechanism: Digital platforms must contribute **1 to 2 percent of their annual turnover** to a dedicated Social Security Fund for these workers. This fund will provide life/disability cover, health benefits, and old-age protection.

core_concepts.title: The Inspector-cum-Facilitator (OSH Code)
core_concepts.description:
A major paradigm shift in administrative law aimed at ending the dreaded 'Inspector Raj'.
- The Transition: The traditional 'Labour Inspector' is abolished. The new authority is the 'Inspector-cum-Facilitator'. 
- The Mandate: Their primary duty is no longer to conduct surprise raids and penalize, but to proactively supply information and **advise employers and workers** on how to comply with safety and health standards. They conduct web-based, randomized inspections rather than discretionary physical raids.

core_concepts.title: Redefining Inter-State Migrant Workers
core_concepts.description:
Under the OSH Code, the definition of an Inter-State Migrant Worker has been massively expanded.
- Old Law: Only covered workers brought in through a middleman/contractor.
- New Law: Now covers workers who are **directly recruited** by the employer from another state, or those who migrate on their own to seek employment, provided they earn up to **₹18,000 per month**. They are guaranteed a yearly journey allowance to visit their hometown.

core_concepts.title: Decriminalization of Offenses
core_concepts.description:
To foster a business-friendly environment, the Codes decriminalize numerous procedural defaults.
- The Mechanism: Offenses that do not involve malicious intent (*mens rea*) or severe bodily harm have been converted from criminal imprisonment to **civil compounding (monetary fines)**. Jail time is strictly reserved for subsequent repeat offenses or violations leading to death/injury.

important_entities.name: National Social Security Board
important_entities.key_fact: The apex body for unorganized welfare.
important_entities.significance: Constituted under the Social Security Code, this Board is specifically tasked with recommending and monitoring welfare schemes for unorganized workers, gig workers, and platform workers. It explicitly mandates the representation of gig workers and aggregators on the board.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do Gig Workers get basic minimum wage protections and union rights under the new Codes? **NO**. This is a massive distinction. The Codes explicitly classify them separately from 'employees'. They receive benefits ONLY under the Code on Social Security. They do NOT fall under the Code on Wages (no minimum wage) or the Industrial Relations Code (no right to form statutory trade unions).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 1 to 2 percent of Turnover, capped at 5 percent of Worker Payable.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Memorize this exact formula for the Social Security Fund contribution mandated for tech aggregators.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Mains (GS 2 or 3), when evaluating India's response to the digital economy, heavily cite the **Code on Social Security, 2020**, noting that while it pioneers the 1-2 percent turnover contribution for gig workers, it deliberately stops short of granting them full 'employee' status.
